blocks.title: Soil
blocks.md: Soil is a mixture of **mineral particles** (rock fragments: **sand**, silt, **clay**), **organic matter** (humus from dead plants and animals), **water**, **air** and living organisms (earthworms, bacteria, fungi). **Loam**, a mixture of sand, silt and clay with humus, is best for most crops: it holds water yet drains well and contains air.

figure.unit: % by volume in a typical loam (approximate)

blocks.caption: Composition of a typical loam (varies with the soil).
blocks.alt: A bar chart: mineral particles about 45 percent, organic matter 5 percent, water 25 percent and air 25 percent.

blocks.title: Sand and clay
blocks.md:
- **Sandy soil**: large particles, drains quickly, dry, low in nutrients, easy to dig.
- **Clay soil**: tiny particles, holds water and can become water-logged, sticky and hard to dig, rich in minerals.
- **Humus** improves structure, holds water and releases mineral ions as it is decomposed.

blocks.title: Soil fertility and the nitrogen cycle
blocks.md: Plants need **nitrates** (nitrogen), **phosphates** and **potassium**. Nitrogen gas in the air cannot be used by plants. **Nitrogen-fixing bacteria** (free in the soil, or in the **root nodules** of legumes such as beans and groundnuts) change it into nitrogen compounds; **nitrifying bacteria** make nitrates. **Decomposers** release ammonium from dead matter; **denitrifying bacteria** return some nitrogen to the air.

blocks.caption: A simplified nitrogen cycle.
blocks.alt: Six boxes: nitrogen gas in air, nitrogen-fixing bacteria, nitrates in soil, plants take up nitrates, animals eat plants, decomposers return nitrates.

blocks.title: Keeping soil fertile
blocks.md:
- **Manure and compost** (organic fertilisers) add humus and slowly release minerals; **chemical fertilisers** (NPK) give fast nutrients but may wash into rivers.
- **Crop rotation** including legumes restores nitrogen.
- **Mulching** (a layer of leaves or straw) reduces evaporation and erosion; **fallow** lets the soil recover.
- **Contour planting and terraces** (on hills) and keeping cover reduce **erosion**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Clay soil holds the *most* water; sandy soil drains fastest.
- Plants cannot use nitrogen gas directly; they need nitrates.
- Chemical fertiliser is not 'bad' in itself: the problem is applying too much, which pollutes rivers.

blocks.title: Water content of a soil sample
blocks.statement: A 50 g sample of fresh soil is dried in an oven until its mass stays constant at 40 g. Calculate the percentage of water.

blocks.title: Air in soil
blocks.statement: 100 cm³ of dry soil is poured into 100 cm³ of water. The final volume is 180 cm³. Find the volume and percentage of air in the soil.
steps: Expected total without air: 200 cm³; observed: 180 cm³.
Air displaced by water = 200 − 180 = 20 cm³, so 20 ÷ 100 × 100 = 20 % of the soil volume.
